text:
Maya: Quick q — how should the gateway treat overlapping wildcard host+path when a header override is present? e.g., `Host: api.*` vs `Host: *.internal` and path `/v1/*` with header `x-service: billing`
Alejandra: Historically we match host -> path -> other predicates. Header overrides were treated as lower priority (they were intended as tie-breakers)
Sam: That ordering is causing real ambiguity for split-host deployments. If a client sets x-service, they expect routing to that service to win in many cases.
Kai: We should be careful changing global precedence. Breaking existing behavior will surprise customers. Maybe add an explicit opt-in for header-driven overrides.
Lucas: Alternative: extend the route grammar to accept an explicit `priority` number per route and evaluate by that first, then fall back to specificity rules (host specificity -> path specificity -> creation_time)
Maya: Draft example that shows the problem and a couple of potential syntaxes:
```
# current implicit style (ambiguous)
- match:
    - host: "*.redwood.com"
    - path: "/v1/*"
  service: accounts

- match:
    - host: "api.redwood.com"
    - path: "/v1/*"
    - header: {name: "x-service", value: "billing"}
  service: billing

# explicit priority approach
- match:
    - host: "*.redwood.com"
    - path: "/v1/*"
  service: accounts
  priority: 10

- match:
    - host: "api.redwood.com"
    - path: "/v1/*"
    - header: {name: "x-service", value: "billing"}
  service: billing
  priority: 50
```
Alejandra: I like explicit `priority`, but need migration story. Also think we should allow a flag `headerOverlays: true` so headers only act as high-priority when routes opt in
dev-bot: route-compiler tests: 42/128 failing (see CI: https://ci.internal/redwood/routes) :warning:
Sam: Non-breaking extension idea: 1) default behavior unchanged, 2) new field `headerOverlays: true` or `priority` for routes. 3) Console UX shows when two routes are ambiguous and lets users resolve
Kai: Also add a deterministic tie-breaker doc: when priorities equal -> host specificity (exact > wildcard) -> path specificity (longer literal segments > shorter) -> header specificity -> created_at
Lucas: I'll run the matcher fuzzer on current config and collect examples where header should logically win but doesn't.
Maya: Can someone take the RFC? I'll draft examples and broken-case reproducer. @Sam @Alejandra
Sam: I'll add unit tests for: ambiguous host-wildcards, header-overrides, explicit priority. Will push tests to branch `route-priority-rfc`. :thumbsup:
Alejandra: I'll outline migration notes and console UX copy (warnings/confirmations)
Kai: +1 on docs. Also let's record this in the gateway changelog so customers know the opt-in semantics
Lucas: Running quick experiment now, will post results in this thread in a few mins
Maya: Thanks all — capturing action items: Maya draft RFC + reproducer, Sam tests, Alejandra migration + UX, Lucas matcher fuzzing. We'll sync tomorrow 11am. :calendar:
